title: Your mind can actively juggle only about four things at once
body: Working memory is the mental workspace that holds information you are actively using, like a number you are about to type. In 1956 George Miller famously put its limit at ‘seven, plus or minus two’ items, but later work, notably by Nelson Cowan, suggests the core capacity is closer to about four chunks for young adults. We stretch it by chunking, grouping items into meaningful units, which is why FBI is easier to hold than F, B and I.
